question: Do standard first-jet covectors from two Ramanujan-Sato formulas outside one quadratic signature orbit admit nontrivial dual-jet orbit invariants?

selected_formulas.label: signature-4-level-2-degree-29
selected_formulas.source: Guillera arXiv:1911.03968 and parent research unit

theorems.statement: For nonzero analytic germs at nonzero basepoints, fixed nonzero scalar K, and B1*B2 != 0, an unrestricted local analytic coordinate/gauge arrow exists carrying any normalized first-jet formula c1*j1=K to any other c2*j2=K.
construction: B components agree by construction; A components agree because both pairings equal K and F2(w2) != 0
theorems.consequence: At fixed K != 0 there are exactly two unrestricted first-jet orbits, B=0 and B!=0.

theorems.statement: Within Gauss period systems with two parabolic singularities and one finite-order elliptic singularity, the odd part of the projective elliptic monodromy order is invariant under chains of quadratic equation-preserving pullbacks, scalar gauges, and reverse traversal of those quadratic relations.
The a=1/4 and a=1/3 period systems lie in distinct quadratic equation-pullback components because their elliptic projective monodromy orders are 2 and 3, with odd parts 1 and 3.

key_negative_result: A first-order coefficient-level orbit invariant cannot distinguish the selected formulas unless the arrow category retains differential-equation/local-system provenance.
minimal_rigidified_object: (Gauss period local system, Clausen rank-3 operator, chosen solution, basepoint, covector, scalar normalization)
scope_boundaries: The manufactured first-jet arrow is local and tautological; it is not modular and does not intertwine the differential equations.
The quadratic separation concerns equation-preserving pullback chains, not arbitrary correspondences represented by a common-cover span.
A common third cover may still relate the two systems bivariantly; this requires separate span and holonomy analysis.
No P000 six-dimensional lift is determined by these rank-2/rank-3 results.
